# `<vector.h>`

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_docs.py in kagantmr/zuzu. Do not edit. -->

Type-safe growable arrays, generated per element type by DEFINE_VEC().

```c
#include <vector.h>
```

## Constants

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="vec_alloc"></a>`VEC_ALLOC(sz)` |  | Allocates zeroed memory: KZAlloc() in the kernel, malloc() in userspace. |
| <a id="vec_free"></a>`VEC_FREE(ptr)` |  | Frees memory from VEC_ALLOC(). |
| <a id="vec_alloc_t"></a>`VEC_ALLOC_T(type, count)` |  | Allocates an array of `count` elements of `type`. |
| <a id="vec_initial_cap"></a>`VEC_INITIAL_CAP` | `16` | Capacity of a new vector. |
| <a id="define_vec"></a>`DEFINE_VEC(name, type)` |  | Defines a vector type for elements of `type`, and its functions. Generates: - `name##_vec_t`: { type *data; uint32_t len; uint32_t cap; } - `bool name##_vec_init(v)`: allocates VEC_INITIAL_CAP zeroed slots; false if out of memory. - `type *name##_vec_get(v, i)`: slot `i`, or NULL if `i` >= cap. Bounds are checked against the capacity, not the length. - `const type *name##_vec_get_const(v, i)`: the same for a const vector. - `int name##_vec_grow(v)`: doubles the capacity, zeroing the new slots; -1 if out of memory. - `void name##_vec_destroy(v)`: frees the storage. - `bool name##_vec_push(v, item)`: appends a copy of *item, growing as needed; false if out of memory. |
